chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When Jibraeel (peace be upon him) descended with the Adhan upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), his head was in the lap of Ali (peace be upon him). So Jibraeel (peace be upon him) called the Adhan and the Iqamah. When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) awoke, he said: 'O Ali, did you hear?' He said: 'Yes'. He said: 'Did you memorize?' He said: 'Yes'. He said: 'Call Bilal and teach him.' So Ali (peace be upon him) called Bilal and taught him.
ai.seo_question: How was the Adhan first taught to the Prophet and transmitted to Bilal?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the intimate spiritual connection between the Prophet and Imam Ali during the inception of the Adhan, underscoring Ali's role as the primary transmitter of this divine liturgy. It establishes the Prophet's direct instruction to Ali to teach Bilal, thereby linking the authority of the call to prayer to the Ahl al-Bayt's custodianship. This narrative reinforces the Shia view of Ali's unique proximity to the Prophet and his pivotal role in establishing Islamic ritual practice.
